theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Which is the best way to greet a guest arriving at the villa?
options: Wave from across the garden and carry on with your work
Smile, look at the guest and say "Good afternoon, welcome"
Wait until the guest speaks first, then just nod your head
Ask straight away how many nights the guest is staying

questions.stem: What is "active listening"?
options: Listening to music while you work, so you stay active
Thinking about your answer while the other person speaks
Talking quickly so the other person cannot interrupt you
Full attention, nodding, and checking you understood

questions.stem: Which body language shows a guest that you are ready to help?
options: Arms folded, while you look down at your phone
Facing the guest, with an open posture and a smile
Leaning on the wall with your hands in your pockets
Turning half away to finish talking to a colleague

questions.stem: A guest speaks quickly and you do not understand the request. What should you do?
options: Ask politely again, then repeat back what you heard
Nod and smile, and then guess what the guest wanted
Tell the guest that their accent is too hard to follow
Walk away and send another worker over to them later

questions.stem: How should you answer the villa phone?
options: Say "Yes?" and wait for the caller to explain what they want
Let it ring until somebody else in the villa picks it up
Greet the caller, give the villa's name and your own name
Answer with "Hold on" and put the phone down on the desk

questions.stem: You take a phone message for the villa manager. What must it include?
options: The caller's name and number, the message, date and time
Only the caller's first name, so the manager can call back
Your own opinion of the caller's voice and manner
Just "somebody called", so the manager can guess who

questions.stem: What does good customer service mean?
options: Doing only the tasks that are written in your job description
Serving the guests who tip the most before all the others
Agreeing with guests even when they ask for unsafe things
Meeting, or going beyond, what the guest needs and expects

questions.stem: Mr and Mrs Brown tell you they are celebrating their anniversary at the villa. What is a good thing to do?
options: Tell every other guest, so that they can congratulate them
Ask them how much they paid for the holiday in total
Tell the manager, so a small surprise can be arranged
Say nothing, since it is not part of your job to know

questions.stem: How can you find out what a guest needs?
options: Guess from the clothes and shoes that the guest is wearing
Ask open questions and listen carefully to the answers
Wait until the guest complains about something missing
Ask other guests at the villa what this guest likes

questions.stem: Which of these is an open question?
options: What would you like to do tomorrow?
Do you want a taxi to the beach?
Is the room all right for you?
Shall I bring some water now?

questions.stem: A guest who uses a wheelchair arrives. What is the best first step?
options: Push the wheelchair without asking, to save the guest effort
Speak only to the guest's companion and not to the guest
Speak loudly and slowly, as if the guest cannot hear
Ask the guest how you can help, and listen to the answer

questions.stem: An elderly guest finds the villa steps hard to climb. What should you do?
options: Tell the guest to try taking the steps faster next time
Leave the guest to manage, since they did not ask for help
Offer help, and ask the manager about a ground-floor room
Pick the guest up and carry them up the steps without asking

questions.stem: A guest asks you something you do not know the answer to. What should you do?
options: Say you will find out, then come back with the answer
Make up an answer so that you do not look foolish
Tell the guest it is not your job to know about that
Change the subject and hope that the guest forgets

questions.stem: A guest complains loudly that the air conditioning is not working. What should you do first?
options: Tell the guest firmly to stop shouting at you
Listen without interrupting, and stay calm
Explain that it is the maintenance team's fault
Walk away until the guest has calmed down

questions.stem: Which is the best thing to say to a guest who has a complaint?
options: "Sorry, but it's not my fault, so I can't help you."
"Other guests have never complained about this."
"You should have told us about this yesterday."
"I'm sorry this happened. Let me sort it out for you."

questions.stem: After you have put right a guest's complaint, what should you do?
options: Keep away from that guest for the rest of their stay
Ask the guest not to complain about anything again
Check back later that the guest is now happy
Add the cost of the repair to the guest's bill

questions.stem: A guest's complaint is about something you cannot fix yourself. What should you do?
options: Say that nothing can be done, and leave it at that
Tell your supervisor quickly and keep the guest informed
Promise a full refund, even though you cannot give one
Ask the guest to write a letter of complaint to the owner

questions.stem: A guest is rude and swears at you. What should you do?
options: Stay calm and polite; get your supervisor if it goes on
Swear back, so that the guest knows how it feels
Refuse to serve the guest again, without telling anyone
Tell the other guests how rude this guest has been

questions.stem: Guests from many countries stay at the villa. How should you treat them?
options: Give the best service to guests from your favourite country
Treat everyone the same and ignore their different customs
With equal respect, while learning about their customs
Keep away from guests who do not speak English well

questions.stem: What is the main benefit of good teamwork at a villa?
options: Each worker can do less work and leave earlier
The supervisor never needs to check anything
Staff can choose only the jobs they like to do
Work is done well and guests get better service

questions.stem: A colleague in the kitchen is very busy and you have finished your own tasks. What should you do?
options: Offer to help with tasks you are trained to do
Take a long break, since your own work is done
Tell the colleague to hurry up and work faster
Go home early without telling the supervisor

questions.stem: Why is a handover important at the end of a shift?
options: It lets the last shift leave without cleaning up
The next shift learns what is done and still to do
It gives staff time to chat about their weekend
It is only needed when the manager is at the villa

questions.stem: What should a good handover note include?
options: The names of the guests who gave the best tips
Complaints about colleagues you do not get on with
Guest requests, unfinished jobs and any problems
Only the time that you left the villa that day

questions.stem: Kemar is new on the team and does not know where the cleaning supplies are kept. What should you do?
options: Laugh and tell him that he should know by now
Tell him to go and ask one of the guests
Ignore him, so that he learns on his own
Show him where they are and explain the system

questions.stem: Your supervisor gives you an instruction you do not fully understand. What should you do?
options: Ask questions until you are sure, before you start
Start the job and guess the parts you are not sure about
Ask one of the guests what the supervisor meant
Do a different job instead and say nothing about it

questions.stem: Your supervisor says your beds are not made to the villa's standard. How should you respond?
options: Argue that your way is better and refuse to change it
Listen, ask how to improve, and practise the right way
Complain to the guests about how strict the supervisor is
Stop making beds, so that somebody else has to do them

questions.stem: Tanisha and Dwayne argue about whose turn it is to clean the pool. What is the best way to settle it?
options: Shout at each other until one of them gives in
Leave the pool dirty until the manager notices
Talk calmly, check the roster and agree what is fair
Ask the guests to vote on who should clean it

questions.stem: Why should staff never argue in front of guests?
options: Guests are not allowed to hear the staff speak at all
It is fine, as long as the argument is kept quiet
Arguments are only a problem when they are in the kitchen
It upsets guests and harms the villa's good name

questions.stem: What is the best way to pass a guest's special request to a colleague?
options: Shout it across the garden to them as you walk past
Tell them clearly and write it down as well
Hope that they hear about it from the guest instead
Mention it a week later, whenever you remember it

questions.stem: When you explain something to a visitor, why is it best to use clear, simple English instead of local slang?
options: So the visitor fully understands what you mean
Because local slang is against the law at work
Because visitors only understand very formal words
Because local words are always rude to visitors

questions.stem: Why does a friendly, positive attitude matter when working with guests?
options: It means you never need to do any real work
It lets you get away with not following the rules
It makes guests feel welcome and valued
It only matters on the days that guests tip

questions.stem: You are having a bad day at home. How should you behave with guests?
options: Tell the guests your problems, so they understand your mood
Avoid all of the guests until you feel better again
Be short with the guests so that they leave you alone
Keep your problems private and stay professional

questions.stem: A guest by the pool asks for extra towels. What is the best response?
options: Say "Certainly" and bring them promptly
Say that towels are only for the bathrooms
Point to the laundry room so they can fetch them
Say yes, then bring them at the end of your shift

questions.stem: Why should you use a guest's name when you speak to them?
options: It proves that you have read the guest's passport
It makes the guest feel recognised and valued
It lets the other guests know who is staying
It is the only way to get the guest's attention

questions.stem: A family asks you to recommend a place to eat in Negril. What should you do?
options: Send them only to your cousin's restaurant in town
Tell them all places outside the villa are unsafe
Give honest ideas that suit their tastes and budget
Tell them you know nothing about places in Negril

questions.stem: A guest slips and falls by the pool. What should you do first?
options: Ask the guest to sign a form before you help them
Finish your own task first, then go and have a look
Lift the guest up at once, even if they are hurt
Make the area safe and call for trained help at once

questions.stem: What does "exceeding expectations" mean?
options: Giving better service than the guest expected
Charging more than the guest expected to pay
Taking longer to serve than the guest expected
Doing less than the guest asked you to do

questions.stem: Why should a villa ask guests for feedback?
options: To find out which staff to dismiss each month
To collect guests' home addresses for adverts
To learn what is going well and what to improve
To give guests something to do on the last day

questions.stem: What is a team briefing at the start of the day for?
options: To give out the pay slips for the week
To share the day's plans, guest needs and tasks
To choose who will take the next day off
To let staff complain about the guests

questions.stem: Which of these shows respect for your colleagues?
options: Leaving your dirty dishes for others to wash
Talking about a colleague behind their back
Taking the credit for work a colleague did
Being on time and sharing the work fairly

questions.stem: You need to move a heavy box of supplies. What should you do?
options: Lift it alone and quickly, so nobody sees you struggle
Ask one of the guests to help you carry it
Ask a colleague to help, and lift it together safely
Leave it in the doorway until somebody else moves it

questions.stem: A guest asks for a vegetarian meal. What does this usually mean?
options: No meat, poultry or fish
No vegetables at all
Only raw fruit
No salt or sugar

questions.stem: What is the best way to end a conversation with a guest?
options: Walk off as soon as you have finished speaking
Thank them and ask if there is anything else
Tell them you are too busy to talk any longer
Say goodbye while you look at your phone

questions.stem: A guest speaks very little English. Which is the most helpful approach?
options: Shout, so that the guest can hear you better
Avoid the guest and wait for somebody else to help
Speak faster, so the conversation is over sooner
Speak slowly, using simple words and gestures

questions.stem: Why do villas set service standards, such as answering the phone within three rings?
options: So that workers can be fined each time they miss one
So that guests have something to complain about
So every guest gets the same good service each time
So that staff do not need any training at all

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the name for the messages we send without words, such as facial expressions and posture?
What do you call a guest who comes back to stay at the same villa again and again?
What is the name of the written timetable that shows which staff work which shifts?
What is the name of the book in which staff write notes and requests for the next shift?
Putting things right for a guest after something has gone wrong is called "service ___". What is the missing word?
What is the word for understanding and sharing how another person feels?
What do you call the written record of a guest complaint and how it was solved?

What kind of app on a phone can help you understand a guest who speaks another language?
What word describes a group of people working together towards the same goal?

essays.stem: Describe how you would use spoken words and body language to make a guest feel welcome when they arrive at a villa.
essays.modelAnswer: When the guest's car arrives, I would stop what I am doing, walk towards them, smile and make friendly eye contact, because body language is the first thing the guest notices. I would stand up straight with an open posture, hands out of my pockets, in a clean uniform. I would greet them warmly with the time of day, for example "Good afternoon, Mr Grant, welcome to Seagrape Villa," using their name if I know it, and introduce myself. I would speak clearly, at a calm pace and in a friendly tone, using simple words. I would offer to help with the luggage and offer a cool welcome drink. While showing them around, I would listen carefully, nod, and ask open questions about their journey and their plans. I would end by telling them how to contact me and wishing them a pleasant stay.
markingPoints: Stops work, approaches, smiles and makes eye contact
Open posture and a neat, professional appearance
Warm greeting with the time of day and the guest's name; introduces self
Clear, friendly tone and simple words; listens and asks open questions
Offers help (luggage, drink) and explains how to get help during the stay

essays.stem: Explain how you would find out and meet the needs of a family with young children staying at a villa.
essays.modelAnswer: I would read the booking notes before they arrive and check for any special requests, such as a cot, a high chair or allergies. When they arrive, I would greet the whole family, including the children, and ask the parents open questions, such as "What do the children like to eat?" and "What would you like to do during your stay?" I would listen carefully and write the answers down for the team. To meet their needs, I would make sure the cot and high chair are clean and safe, and offer meals that children enjoy at times that suit them. I would point out safety points such as the pool gate and the steps, and remind the parents that children must always be watched near water. I would suggest family activities and trips that suit the children's ages. During the stay I would check that the family is happy, and pass any new requests to my supervisor.
markingPoints: Checks the booking and special requests before arrival
Asks open questions, listens and records the answers for the team
Prepares suitable, safe equipment and child-friendly meals
Points out safety risks (pool, steps) and the need to watch children near water
Suggests suitable activities and follows up during the stay

essays.stem: Describe the steps you would follow to handle a guest complaint, using an example from villa work.
essays.modelAnswer: For example, a guest complains that the hot water in her bathroom is not working. First, I would listen to her without interrupting, give her my full attention and stay calm. Second, I would apologise sincerely: "I'm very sorry about this, Mrs Thompson." I would not make excuses or blame anyone. Third, I would show I understand by repeating the problem back to her, and ask any questions I need. Fourth, I would act: tell her what I will do and how long it should take, report it at once to my supervisor and the maintenance staff, and offer another bathroom she can use in the meantime. Fifth, I would follow up: check later that the hot water is working and that she is happy. Last, I would record the complaint and what was done, so the villa can stop it happening again.
markingPoints: Listens calmly without interrupting
Apologises sincerely without excuses or blame
Checks understanding by repeating the problem back
Acts: explains what will happen and when, reports it, offers an alternative
Follows up with the guest and records the complaint

essays.stem: Explain how you would deal with an angry or rude guest, while keeping yourself and others safe.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would stay calm and keep my voice low and polite, even if the guest is shouting, because an angry reply only makes things worse. I would try not to take it personally. I would listen to find out what has upset the guest, and show that I understand, for example: "I can see this has really upset you." Where I can, I would move the conversation away from other guests to a quieter but open place, so others are not disturbed. I would apologise for the problem and say what I can do to fix it. I would not argue, swear back or touch the guest. If the guest keeps being abusive or threatens anyone, I would keep a safe distance, stay near other staff, and call my supervisor or security at once, and the police if there is violence. Afterwards I would write a report of what happened.
markingPoints: Stays calm and polite and does not take it personally
Listens and shows understanding
Moves the talk away from other guests to a quiet but open place
Apologises and offers a solution; never argues, swears or touches
Keeps a safe distance and calls the supervisor, security or police if needed; writes a report

essays.stem: Explain why teamwork is important in a villa, and describe what a good team member does.
essays.modelAnswer: In a villa, housekeepers, cooks, butlers, gardeners and drivers all depend on each other. If one person does not do their part, the guest notices: a room is not ready, or dinner is late. Good teamwork means jobs are done well and on time, guests get better service, and work is safer and less stressful. A good team member arrives on time and does their own share of the work well. They communicate clearly, passing on guest requests and writing a good handover. They help colleagues who are busy, once their own tasks are done. They are polite and respectful, avoid gossip, and deal with disagreements calmly and in private. They follow instructions and safety rules, are willing to learn, and accept feedback. They also share ideas to improve the service and give credit to others.
markingPoints: Explains that staff depend on each other and guests notice when one fails
Is on time and does their own share of the work well
Communicates clearly: passes on requests and writes a good handover
Helps busy colleagues and shares ideas
Is respectful, handles disagreements calmly, follows instructions and accepts feedback

essays.stem: Describe what a good shift handover includes, and why it matters for guests and colleagues.
essays.modelAnswer: A shift handover is when the staff finishing a shift pass important information to the staff starting the next one. A good handover is done face to face where possible and also written down, so nothing is forgotten. It includes guest requests and special needs, such as a late check-out, an early breakfast or an allergy; jobs that are not finished and what is still to be done; problems or faults, such as a broken light or a pool pump not working, and whether they have been reported; complaints and how they were dealt with; and expected arrivals, departures and deliveries. It matters because guests should not have to repeat themselves, and the service should be smooth at all hours. It helps colleagues plan their work, avoids mistakes, and keeps everyone safe, because hazards are passed on.
markingPoints: Explains what a handover is
Done face to face and in writing
Includes guest requests, unfinished jobs, faults, complaints and expected arrivals
Guests do not have to repeat themselves and service stays smooth
Helps colleagues plan, avoids mistakes and passes on hazards

essays.stem: Two colleagues keep arguing about the work roster. Describe how the conflict could be solved.
essays.modelAnswer: First, the argument should stop in front of guests and move to a private place at a suitable time, such as after lunch service. Each colleague should have the chance to explain their side calmly while the other listens without interrupting. They should talk about the problem, the roster, and not attack each other personally. Together they should look at the facts: what the roster says, how the shifts have been shared, and any personal needs such as childcare or transport. Then they can suggest solutions, such as swapping shifts or taking turns at weekends, and agree on one that is fair to both. If they cannot agree, they should ask their supervisor to help, since the supervisor is responsible for the roster. The agreement should be written down, and the supervisor should check after a week or two that it is working.
markingPoints: Moves the discussion to a private place, away from guests
Each side is heard calmly; they talk about the problem, not the person
They check the facts (roster, shifts shared, personal needs)
They suggest options and agree a fair solution
The supervisor helps if needed; the agreement is recorded and reviewed

essays.stem: Describe how to handle a phone call to the villa professionally, from answering it to passing on a message.
essays.modelAnswer: I would answer within a few rings, smile as I speak, and greet the caller: "Good morning, Seagrape Villa, Keisha speaking. How may I help you?" I would speak clearly, at a steady pace and in a friendly tone, and listen carefully, taking notes. If the call is for someone who is not available, I offer to take a message. I write down the caller's name, checking the spelling, their phone number, the date and time, and the message, then read it back to check it is right. I never tell a caller a guest's room or plans; I take a message for the guest instead. If I need to put the caller on hold, I ask first and come back to them quickly. I end the call politely and thank the caller. Then I pass the message on straight away, to the right person.
markingPoints: Answers promptly with a greeting, the villa's name and own name
Speaks clearly and politely, listens and takes notes
Takes a full message (name, number, date, time, message) and reads it back
Protects guest privacy and uses hold correctly
Ends politely and passes the message on promptly

essays.stem: Explain how you would serve a guest who has difficulty hearing and a guest who speaks little English.
essays.modelAnswer: For the guest who has difficulty hearing, I would face them when I speak, so they can see my face and lips, and make sure there is good light and little background noise. I would speak clearly at a normal pace, without shouting, and use short sentences. I would check that they understood, and write down important details such as times and phone numbers. I would ask how they prefer to communicate, and tell my colleagues so the whole team can help. For the guest who speaks little English, I would speak slowly with simple words and avoid slang. I would use gestures, pictures, maps and written notes, and a translation app on the phone if needed. I would ask whether a colleague speaks their language. With both guests I would be patient and friendly, never laugh or show annoyance, and check understanding by asking them to show me or repeat back.
markingPoints: Hearing: faces the guest, with good light and little noise
Hearing: speaks clearly without shouting, writes details down, asks how they prefer to communicate
Little English: speaks slowly with simple words and no slang
Little English: uses gestures, pictures, a translation app or a colleague who speaks the language
Is patient with both and checks understanding

essays.stem: Explain how you should receive instructions and feedback from a supervisor, and why this helps you improve.
essays.modelAnswer: When I receive an instruction, I stop what I am doing, listen carefully, and make notes if it is long. I ask questions if anything is not clear, and repeat the main points back, so we both know I have understood. If I cannot do the task, for example because I am not trained or do not have the right equipment, I say so straight away instead of guessing. Then I carry it out properly and on time, and report back when it is done. When my supervisor gives me feedback, I listen without arguing or making excuses, even if it is critical. I thank them, ask how I can do better, and practise the right way. I also accept praise politely. This helps me improve because I learn the villa's standards, avoid repeating mistakes, build my skills and confidence, and earn trust for more responsibility.
markingPoints: Listens carefully and makes notes
Asks questions and repeats the instruction back
Says at once if they cannot do the task; reports back when done
Accepts feedback without arguing and asks how to improve
Explains how this builds skills, avoids repeated mistakes and earns trust

practical1.title: Role-play a guest arrival, a special request and a complaint, and record each one
practical1.brief: The assessor plays a villa guest (or chooses trainees to play guests) and gives your group three situations: welcoming a guest family on arrival; a guest with a special request (for example, a birthday cake, or a guest who speaks little English); and a guest complaint (for example, no hot water). For each situation, one or two members play the villa staff while the others watch and note good points. After each role play, the staff member writes the request or complaint in the log book or on the complaint form, and hands it over to a 'colleague' (another member), who reads it back and says what they will do. Swap roles so that every member plays staff in at least one situation and writes at least one record. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group, with the log entries and the complaint form.
materials: A simple villa reception set-up: a table, chairs, a phone, and a welcome tray with glasses of water or juice
A log book or message pad, and a guest complaint form
Pens, a clipboard, and a phone or tablet for photos
photos: The group's plan: who plays each part
The arrival role play, showing the greeting
The complaint role play, showing the staff member listening
The log book entry and the completed complaint form
The request being handed over to a 'colleague'
checklist: Greeted the guest warmly, with a smile, eye contact and the guest's name
Used clear, polite words and open, friendly body language
Listened actively and checked understanding by repeating back
Handled the complaint: listened, apologised, acted and followed up
Wrote a clear, accurate record with the date, time, guest name and action taken
Passed information to a colleague clearly and supported the team
Gave respectful comments on other members' role plays
safety: Role plays use words only: no pushing or grabbing
Keep drinks away from paperwork and wipe spills at once
Use made-up guest names, never real ones
Any member may stop a role play if they feel uncomfortable

practical2.title: Run a team briefing, prepare a villa for a guest arrival, and hand over to the next shift
practical2.brief: Your group is the villa team getting ready for a family of four arriving this afternoon. First write a simple duty plan showing each member's tasks, for example: the welcome area and drinks, a guest information sheet about the villa and the local area, checking the bedroom and bathroom, and the arrival greeting. One member leads a 10-minute team briefing to share the plan and the guests' needs (given by the assessor). Then carry out the tasks as a team, helping each other once a task is finished. Last, write a handover sheet for the next shift and hand it over face to face to the assessor. Every member must have a task, take part in the briefing, and add at least one item to the handover sheet. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group, with the duty plan, the information sheet and the handover sheet.
materials: A guest details card from the assessor (names, arrival time, special needs)
Paper, pens, markers and a clipboard
A villa room or the Centre's training room, with bed linen and towels
A welcome tray, jug, glasses, and juice or water
A phone or tablet for photos
photos: The written duty plan, showing each member's task
Members working on their tasks, including helping each other
The welcome area and the guest information sheet
The bedroom and bathroom ready for the guests
The handover sheet and the face-to-face handover
checklist: Took part in the duty plan and understood their own task
Listened and spoke up during the briefing
Did their task well and on time
Offered help to others once their own task was done
Spoke politely and clearly with team members
Added accurate information to the handover sheet
Helped leave the area clean and tidy
safety: Lift linen and boxes safely, and ask for help with heavy items
Keep floors dry and walkways clear; put out a wet-floor sign after mopping
Wash hands before handling glasses and drinks
Follow the Centre's rules for any cleaning chemicals: read the label, wear gloves and never mix products
